title: A nonnullable PHPDoc return contradicts an actually nullable return

ground_truth.statement: The native nullable signature permits null, and the false branch actually returns it. The @return stdClass annotation is therefore too narrow. The caller's null check is necessary, not a redundant condition.

provenance.note: Read actual valid-provider dataset. Preserved the conflicting PHPDoc/native signatures but replaced randomness with a bool parameter. Upstream validity is not used as truth for the contradictory annotation.

notes: All three tools emit no diagnostics. Retained as FN against the literal nonnullable PHPDoc contract, not advertised as three runtime-safety defects: the native signature is correct and tools may deliberately merge native null into the documented type. No affirmative non-support policy was established, so none is marked unsupported. Runtime proves guarded() can return both true and false.
